1.headline: The United States will stop giving money to Israel
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's news is about the United States and Israel. Every year, the United States gives Israel help. This help is worth four billion dollars.
On Tuesday, President Donald Trump spoke to a TV news channel. He said this help will stop next year. He said Israel does not need the money now.
But Israel can still buy weapons from the United States. Weapons are things for fighting, like guns.
Israel's army fought in Gaza and Lebanon. After that, many Americans argued about this help. Now it may end.
Again, the United States plans to stop giving Israel four billion dollars a year. Israel can still buy weapons.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 뉴스는 미국과 이스라엘에 관한 것입니다. 미국은 해마다 이스라엘을 돕습니다. 이 지원은 40억 달러 규모입니다.
화요일에 도널드 트럼프 대통령이 한 TV 뉴스 채널과 이야기했습니다. 그는 이 지원이 내년에 끝난다고 말했습니다. 이스라엘은 이제 그 돈이 필요 없다고 말했습니다.
하지만 이스라엘은 여전히 미국에서 무기를 살 수 있습니다. 무기는 총처럼 싸움에 쓰는 물건입니다.

다시 말씀드리면, 미국은 이스라엘에 해마다 주던 40억 달러를 그만 주려고 합니다. 이스라엘은 여전히 무기를 살 수 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Trump says US aid to Israel will end next year
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Our first story is about money between the United States and Israel. Every year, the United States gives Israel four billion dollars in aid. Aid means help, like money or goods, from one country to another.

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump talked with Fox News by phone. He said this aid will stop next year. He said Israel does not need it anymore. He also said it is a lot of money for the United States.

Trump said Israel's leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, first brought up the idea. He said the two men talked about it for a couple of years. Israel can still buy weapons from the United States. So the two countries will keep doing business.

Why is this important? For many years, the United States sent Israel a lot of military help. But after Israel's wars in Gaza and Lebanon, many Americans started to argue about it. Trump did not say what Congress will do. Congress is the group that makes American laws.
To sum up, Trump says American aid to Israel will end next year. But weapon sales will continue.
Thank you for listening.

화요일에 도널드 트럼프 대통령은 폭스 뉴스와 전화로 이야기했습니다. 그는 이 원조가 내년에 끝난다고 말했습니다. 이스라엘은 더 이상 원조가 필요 없다고 말했습니다. 또 미국에게는 큰돈이라고도 말했습니다.

정리하면, 트럼프 대통령은 이스라엘에 대한 미국의 원조가 내년에 끝난다고 말합니다. 하지만 무기 판매는 계속됩니다.

3.headline: Trump says the US will end yearly aid to Israel in 2027
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's top story is about the United States and Israel. President Donald Trump says the United States will stop giving Israel four billion dollars in aid every year. Aid means money or help that one country gives to another. According to news reports, Trump said this in a phone interview with Fox News on Tuesday. He said the aid will end next year, in 2027.

Trump said Israel does not need the money anymore. He also said it is a lot of money for the United States to spend. He said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu first brought up the idea, and that the two leaders had talked about it for a couple of years. However, the United States will still sell weapons to Israel. So Israel can keep buying military equipment, but it will pay for it.

Here is some background. The United States has been Israel's closest partner for many years. In recent years, it has sent tens of billions of dollars in military aid. But the aid has become a hot topic in American politics, especially after Israel's military actions in Gaza and Lebanon.

Why does this matter? This is a big change in a long relationship. Trump did not explain what role Congress would play. Congress is the part of the government that makes laws and decides how money is spent. He also did not say how this might affect aid to Egypt and Jordan, two other American partners in the Middle East. Netanyahu's office did not comment right away.
To sum up, President Trump says American aid to Israel will end next year, but weapon sales will continue. Many people will watch how Congress and Israel respond.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Trump says annual US military aid to Israel will end in 2027
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

President Donald Trump says the United States will stop providing Israel with four billion dollars in annual aid, starting next year. In a phone interview with Fox News on Tuesday, Trump said Israel no longer needs the assistance, and he described it as a large sum for American taxpayers. He added that Washington will continue to sell arms to its closest ally in the Middle East.

According to the president, the idea came from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and the two leaders had been discussing it for a couple of years. Trump also suggested the aid had become a political issue at home, saying Democratic candidates were using it as a talking point. Netanyahu's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The announcement marks a significant shift in a decades-long partnership. The United States has provided Israel with tens of billions of dollars in military assistance in recent years. However, support for that aid has become increasingly contentious in American politics, particularly following Israel's military operations in Gaza and Lebanon. For decades, this aid has been seen as a symbol of the close ties between the two countries.

Several key questions remain unanswered. The president did not address what role Congress would play, even though lawmakers control federal spending. He also did not say whether the decision would affect aid to Egypt and Jordan, two other important American partners in the region. If the aid ends, Israel would need to cover the cost of future weapons purchases from its own budget.

To sum up, President Trump says annual American aid to Israel will end in 2027, while arms sales between the two countries will continue. Reactions from Congress and the Israeli government are expected in the coming days, as lawmakers in Washington examine the details.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Trump moves to wind down Israel's $4 billion in annual US aid
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

President Donald Trump says the United States will phase out the roughly four billion dollars in aid it gives Israel each year, with the payments ending in 2027. Speaking to Fox News by phone on Tuesday, the president argued that Israel no longer needs the money and that the sum is a considerable burden on American taxpayers. Crucially, he stressed that the arms pipeline will stay open: Washington will keep selling weapons to its closest Middle Eastern ally.

Trump said the proposal originated with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and that the two had been mulling it over for a couple of years. He also framed the aid as a liability in domestic politics, noting that Democratic candidates had seized on it on the campaign trail. Netanyahu's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

If carried through, the move would upend one of the most enduring pillars of American foreign policy. For decades, the package has been regarded as a tangible symbol of the special relationship between the two countries. Washington has channeled tens of billions of dollars in military assistance to Israel in recent years, much of it since the war in Gaza began in 2023. Yet the aid has grown increasingly divisive in the United States, with Israel's military campaigns in Gaza and Lebanon drawing mounting scrutiny across the political spectrum.

For now, the announcement raises more questions than it answers. The president was silent on the role of Congress, which holds the power of the purse and has traditionally approved such funding. Nor did he spell out whether the shift could ripple out to assistance for Egypt and Jordan, two other linchpins of American strategy in the region. In practical terms, Israel would presumably have to foot the bill for future weapons purchases itself, a change that could strain its defense budget.

To sum up, President Trump intends to end annual American aid to Israel in 2027 while keeping arms sales intact. How Congress and the Israeli government respond will determine whether the plan becomes a genuine turning point or remains a statement of intent.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: Greenland says yes to a safety deal
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Greenland is a very big island. It is near the North Pole. It is part of Denmark.
On Tuesday, Greenland's lawmakers voted on a deal. Lawmakers are people who make the laws. Sixteen people said yes. No one said no.
The deal is with Denmark and the United States. It is about keeping the area safe. The United States can build more army bases there. But Greenland stays with Denmark.
Before this, President Donald Trump wanted the United States to control Greenland. Many people in Greenland did not like that. Greenland's leader said, "Greenland is our country."
Again, Greenland said yes to a safety deal with Denmark and the United States.
Thank you for listening.

그린란드는 아주 큰 섬입니다. 북극 가까이에 있습니다. 그린란드는 덴마크에 속해 있습니다.

이 협정은 덴마크, 미국과 맺는 것입니다. 이 지역을 안전하게 지키는 일에 관한 것입니다. 미국은 그곳에 군사 기지를 더 지을 수 있습니다. 하지만 그린란드는 계속 덴마크에 속합니다.
이전에 도널드 트럼프 대통령은 미국이 그린란드를 차지하기를 원했습니다. 그린란드의 많은 사람들은 그것을 좋아하지 않았습니다. 그린란드 지도자는 "그린란드는 우리의 나라입니다"라고 말했습니다.
다시 말씀드리면, 그린란드는 덴마크, 미국과의 안보 협정에 찬성했습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Greenland approves a security deal with Denmark and the US
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Our next story comes from Greenland. Greenland is a huge island in the Arctic, the cold area near the North Pole. It belongs to Denmark, but it runs many of its own affairs.

On Tuesday, lawmakers in Greenland voted for a security deal. Security means keeping a place safe. The vote was sixteen to zero, and seven lawmakers did not vote. The deal is between Greenland, Denmark and the United States.

The three leaders signed the deal in September in New York. Under the deal, the United States can open more military bases in Greenland. But Greenland will stay under Denmark's control. Denmark's lawmakers will talk about the deal later this month.

Why is this important? For months, President Donald Trump said the United States should control Greenland. This made many people in Greenland and Denmark upset. The new deal may make things calmer. Greenland's leader wrote, "Greenland is our country." But some local people say the deal does not help them much.
To sum up, Greenland approved a security deal with Denmark and the United States. The United States can add more bases there.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Greenland lawmakers approve a security deal with Denmark and the US
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Our next story takes us to the Arctic. Lawmakers in Greenland have approved a security agreement with Denmark and the United States. Greenland is the world's largest island. It is a semiautonomous territory of Denmark. That means it makes many of its own decisions, but it is still part of the Danish kingdom.

According to news reports, the vote took place on Tuesday in Nuuk, Greenland's capital. Sixteen lawmakers voted for the deal, none voted against it, and seven did not take a side. The leaders of the three governments signed the agreement in September, at the United Nations meeting in New York.

So what is in the deal? It allows the United States to have more military bases in Greenland. At the same time, Greenland stays under Danish control. The agreement would still apply even if Greenland becomes independent one day. The deal also says American bases should buy goods and services from Greenland as much as possible.

Here is some background. For months, President Donald Trump said the United States should control Greenland. At one point, he did not rule out using force, but he later backed down. Many people in Greenland and Denmark were worried and angry. The new deal is expected to ease these tensions. Greenland's prime minister wrote, "Greenland is our country." Still, some residents say they see few benefits for local people.
Next, Danish lawmakers will discuss the deal later this month.
To sum up, Greenland has said yes to a security deal that allows more American bases, while keeping the island under Danish control.
Thank you for listening.

들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Greenland ratifies trilateral security pact with Denmark and US
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Lawmakers in Greenland have approved a three-way security agreement with Denmark and the United States, a deal that clears the way for an expanded American military presence on the Arctic island. The vote in Nuuk on Tuesday was sixteen in favor and none against, with seven abstentions.

The agreement, which covers security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, was signed in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York by President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen. It allows for additional American bases while keeping Greenland, a semiautonomous territory, under Danish control. The pact would remain in effect even if Greenland eventually chooses independence. It also requires Washington to award base-related contracts to Greenlandic suppliers to the maximum extent possible.

The vote follows months of pressure from the Trump administration. The president had repeatedly called for the United States to take control of the island, citing national security, and at one stage refused to rule out military force before stepping back. The dispute had caused serious tension between Washington and Copenhagen, two NATO allies. The State Department called the vote another major victory for American national security.

In Greenland, reactions have been mixed. Prime Minister Nielsen wrote that cooperation must respect the island's people and rights, adding, "Greenland is our country." Some residents welcomed an end to the threats, while a local mayor said the deal offers little to communities on the island.
The agreement will take effect once parliamentary procedures in both Greenland and Denmark are complete. Danish lawmakers are scheduled to debate it later this month.
To sum up, Greenland has endorsed a security deal that permits more American bases while preserving Danish sovereignty over the island.
Thank you for listening.

협정은 그린란드와 덴마크 양쪽의 의회 절차가 끝나면 발효됩니다. 덴마크 의원들은 이달 말 이 협정을 논의할 예정입니다.
정리하면, 그린란드는 섬에 대한 덴마크의 주권을 지키면서 미군 기지를 늘리는 안보 협정을 승인했습니다.

5.headline: Greenland signs off on Arctic security pact after months of US pressure
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Greenland's parliament has given its blessing to a trilateral security pact with Denmark and the United States, a move that paves the way for a beefed-up American military footprint on the vast Arctic island while defusing, at least for now, a diplomatic row that had strained relations across the North Atlantic. Lawmakers in the capital, Nuuk, backed the agreement on Tuesday by sixteen votes to none, with seven abstaining.

The accord, which addresses security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, was inked in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly by President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen. Under its terms, Washington may establish additional bases, yet the semiautonomous territory remains firmly under Danish jurisdiction. Notably, the pact is designed to outlast any future bid for independence, and it obliges the United States to source base-related goods and services from Greenlandic suppliers to the maximum extent possible.

The vote caps months of mounting pressure from the White House. President Trump had repeatedly insisted that American control of Greenland was vital to national security, and at one point declined to rule out the use of force, before ultimately backing away from any such threat. The State Department hailed the outcome as another major victory for American national security.

On the island itself, the mood is decidedly mixed. Prime Minister Nielsen struck a defiant note, writing that any cooperation must respect Greenlanders and their rights, and declaring, "Greenland is our country." Some residents expressed relief that the saber-rattling appears to be over, but others remain skeptical; one local mayor argued that the deal serves Denmark and NATO while bringing no tangible benefits to island communities.
The pact will enter into force once both Greenland and Denmark have completed their parliamentary processes, with Danish lawmakers due to take up the matter later this month.

To sum up, Greenland has signed off on a security deal that opens the door to more American bases while leaving Danish sovereignty intact, a compromise that may cool tensions, even if it leaves some islanders unconvinced.
Thank you for listening.

Every year, a group called QS ranks universities in Asia. A ranking is a list from best to worst. The new list came out on Tuesday.
More than half of Korean universities went down on the list. Schools far from Seoul went down the most.

2.headline: Half of Korean universities drop in Asia ranking
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Korea University came twelfth. KAIST returned to the list. Still, no Korean school reached the top ten. The University of Hong Kong was first again.

To sum up, top Korean schools did well, but more than half of Korean universities fell.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: More than half of Korean universities fall in QS Asia ranking
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's Korea story is about universities. On Tuesday, QS, a British company that ranks universities, released its new list of the best universities in Asia. A ranking puts schools in order based on things like research, teaching quality and reputation. Reputation means what other people think of a school.

According to the Korea Herald, the results were mixed for Korea. More than half, or fifty-six percent, of Korean universities that were ranked last year fell this year. Thirty-five percent moved up, and nine percent stayed the same. Schools outside the capital area were hit the hardest. Of sixty-one ranked schools outside Seoul, Incheon and Gyeonggi Province, thirty-eight dropped.

At the top, Korean schools did better. Six Korean universities made the top twenty, second only to mainland China with seven. Yonsei University was the highest Korean school in eleventh place, followed by Korea University in twelfth. KAIST came back to the list after being left out last year. However, no Korean university reached the top ten. The University of Hong Kong took first place for the second year in a row.

Why does this matter? Korea's birth rate is very low, so there are fewer students every year. A senior QS official said this is hurting universities outside the capital region. He also said Korean schools need more international research partners and more teachers from abroad.
To sum up, Korea's top universities stayed strong in the Asia ranking, but more than half of Korean schools fell, especially outside the capital area.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Korean universities slide in QS Asia ranking as regional schools struggle
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

More than half of Korea's universities have slipped in the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia, according to results released on Tuesday by the British higher education analytics firm. The 2027 edition assessed more than one thousand seven hundred institutions across the continent.

According to the Korea Herald, fifty-six percent of previously ranked Korean universities lost ground this year, while thirty-five percent improved and nine percent held steady. The decline was concentrated outside the capital region. Of the sixty-one ranked universities located beyond Seoul, Incheon and Gyeonggi Province, thirty-eight fell, compared with twenty of the forty-two schools in the capital area.

Korea's leading institutions, however, held their own. Six Korean universities placed in Asia's top twenty, second only to mainland China's seven. Yonsei University was the country's highest-ranked school at eleventh, followed by Korea University at twelfth. KAIST returned at fifteenth after being excluded from last year's list, while POSTECH dropped out of the top twenty. For yet another year, no Korean university cracked the top ten, which was dominated by schools from Hong Kong and mainland China, led by the University of Hong Kong.

QS senior vice president Ben Sowter said Korea's best universities remain among the strongest in Asia, but that the wider picture is tougher, as a shrinking student population weighs on enrollment outside the capital. He added that Korea is losing ground to regional rivals in international research collaboration and in hiring foreign faculty.
The results come as Korea grapples with one of the world's lowest birth rates, which is expected to sharply reduce the number of new university students in the coming decades.
To sum up, Korea's top universities kept strong positions in the QS Asia ranking, but most others slipped, with regional schools hit hardest.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

코리아헤럴드에 따르면 지난해 순위에 오른 한국 대학 가운데 56퍼센트가 올해 순위가 떨어졌고, 35퍼센트는 올랐으며, 9퍼센트는 제자리를 지켰습니다. 하락은 수도권 밖에 집중되었습니다. 서울, 인천, 경기도 밖에 있는 순위권 대학 61곳 가운데 38곳이 떨어졌고, 수도권 학교는 42곳 가운데 20곳이 떨어졌습니다.

5.headline: QS Asia rankings: Korea's elite hold firm as regional universities lose ground
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Korea's university sector has turned in a decidedly uneven performance in the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia, with its flagship institutions holding firm near the top even as more than half of the country's ranked schools slid down the table. The 2027 edition, unveiled on Tuesday by the British higher education analytics firm, evaluated more than one thousand seven hundred universities across Asia.

According to the Korea Herald, fifty-six percent of Korean universities that featured in last year's list lost ground, against thirty-five percent that climbed and nine percent that stood still. The pain was felt most acutely beyond the greater Seoul area: of sixty-one ranked universities outside Seoul, Incheon and Gyeonggi Province, thirty-eight slipped, compared with twenty of the forty-two in the capital region.

At the summit of the rankings, however, the picture was considerably brighter. Six Korean universities secured places in Asia's top twenty, a tally surpassed only by mainland China's seven. Yonsei University led the domestic pack in eleventh place, with Korea University hot on its heels in twelfth. KAIST made a comeback at fifteenth after being left off last year's table, though POSTECH tumbled out of the top twenty. The top ten nonetheless remained out of reach, with the University of Hong Kong retaining the crown for a second consecutive year.

Ben Sowter, a senior vice president at QS, said Korea's premier universities rank among the most formidable in the region, but cautioned that further down the table it had been a harder year, as a dwindling pool of students takes its toll on enrollment outside the capital. He singled out international research collaboration and the recruitment of overseas faculty as the two areas where Korea is ceding the most ground to its neighbors.

The findings land against the backdrop of Korea's demographic crunch. With one of the lowest birth rates in the world, the country is bracing for a steep decline in the number of new university entrants over the coming decades, a trend that threatens the very survival of some regional campuses.
To sum up, Korea's elite universities held firm in the QS Asia rankings, but the majority of Korean institutions lost ground, underscoring a widening gap between the capital and the regions.
Thank you for listening.
